ITQAN:v4p347/r20.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p347/r20.speaker: جعفر بن شمس الخلافة
ITQAN:v4p347/r20.claim: Ja'far lists this Qur'anic clause among expressions used proverbially (irsāl al-mathal).
ITQAN:v4p347/r20.anchor: عقد جعفر بن شمس الخلافة في كتاب الآداب بابا في ألفاظ من القرآن جارية مجرى المثل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p22/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p22/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p22/r3.claim: The idols cannot hear because they are inanimate; even hypothetically hearing, they would not answer because they disclaim the worshippers' claim of divinity or cannot benefit them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p22/r3.anchor: لا يسمعوا دعاءكم، لأنهم جماد ولو سمعوا، هذا على سبيل الفرض ما استجابوا لكم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p22/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p22/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p22/r4.claim: The phrase يكفرون بشرككم may describe idols' future disavowal, expressed figuratively as they remain inert while disputants speak; Dhū al-Rumma's poem offers a comparable personification of stones.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p22/r4.anchor: وقوله: يكفرون، يحتمل أن يكون بما يظهر هنالك من جمودها وبطئها عند حركة ناطق،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p22/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p22/r5.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p22/r5.claim: Qatāda and other exegetes take the خبر in ولا ينبئك مثل خبير as God, the truthful knower who guarantees the report's certainty.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p22/r5.anchor: قال قتادة وغيره من المفسرين: الخبير هنا أراد به تعالى نفسه، فهو الخبير الصادق الخبر،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p22/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p22/r6.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p22/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya suggests that the saying may continue the idol passage: nothing like an informed speaker can tell you about the idols' own disavowal of their worshippers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p22/r6.anchor: قال ابن عطية: ويحتمل أن يكون قوله: ولا ينبئك مثل خبير من تمام ذكر الأصنام،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p22/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p22/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p22/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī reads the maxim as saying that only someone who knows the matter can report its truth; the speaker is knowledgeable about the idols.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p22/r7.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: لا يخبرك بالأمر مخبر، هو مثل خبير عالم به،

STUDYQURAN:35:intro/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:intro/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:35:intro/r6.claim: The sūrah’s main focus is God’s oneness as the sole Creator and Sustainer, contrasting divine Power with claims made for idols.
STUDYQURAN:35:intro/r6.anchor: The main focus of the sūrah is upon the Oneness of God as the only Creator and Sustainer of existence

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p263/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p263/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p263/r4.claim: David and Solomon received worldly favors without arrogance, remaining grateful and obedient; they made devils follow them rather than serving devils.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p263/r4.anchor: God granted them with all the favours of this world but they never became arrogant and haughty and remained grateful and obedient to Him.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p263/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p263/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p263/r5.claim: God subordinates devils to those who follow Him, while devils overcome the ungrateful and make them their servants.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p263/r5.anchor: God makes the devils become subservient to those who follow their Lord.

TABATABAI:14:19-34#8/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:19-34#8/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:19-34#8/r2.claim: Iblis’s repudiation parallels the Qur’anic accounts of false gods and leaders disowning those who followed them.
TABATABAI:14:19-34#8/r2.anchor: وهذا الكلام منه تبر من شركهم كما حكى سبحانه تبري كل متبوع باطل من تابعه يوم القيامة

RAZI-FULL:v26p12#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p12#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p12#2/r1.claim: Rāzī refutes the claim that idols confer honor because worshippers can approach, see, and present their needs to them.
RAZI-FULL:v26p12#2/r1.anchor: إبطالا لما كانوا يقولون إن في عبادة الأصنام عزة من حيث القرب منها والنظر إليها وعرض الحوائج عليها

RAZI-FULL:v26p12#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p12#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p12#2/r2.claim: Idols do not hear their callers, whereas God receives and accepts the good word that ascends to Him.

RAZI-FULL:v26p12#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p12#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p12#2/r3.claim: Even granting the idolaters’ belief that idols hear and know, they cannot claim that idols answer prayers, since nonresponse is perceptible while hearing is a rational dispute.
RAZI-FULL:v26p12#2/r3.anchor: فإنهم كانوا يقولون بأن الأصنام تسمع

RAZI-FULL:v26p12#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p12#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p12#2/r4.claim: After establishing idols give no worldly benefit, God shows that they will bring no afterlife benefit and will instead disavow their worshippers’ association.
RAZI-FULL:v26p12#2/r4.anchor: لما بين عدم النفع فيهم في الدنيا بين عدم النفع منهم في الآخرة بل أشار إلى وجود الضرر منهم في الآخرة

RAZI-FULL:v26p12#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p12#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p12#2/r5.claim: Here shirk means associating something with God, as in the description of association as a tremendous wrong.
RAZI-FULL:v26p12#2/r5.anchor: أي بإشراككم بالله شيئا ، كما قال تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v26p12#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p12#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p12#2/r6.claim: One reading addresses the Prophet: God reveals that wood and stone will speak and disavow their worshippers on Judgment Day, something reason alone could not know; the extraordinary report is true because its source is all-knowing.
RAZI-FULL:v26p12#2/r6.anchor: أن الخشب والحجر يوم القيامة ينطق ويكذب عابده وذلك أمر لا يعلم بالعقل المجرد لولا إخبار الله تعالى عنه

RAZI-FULL:v26p12#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p12#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p12#2/r7.claim: Alternatively, the address is general: whoever the listener may be, what has just been related is true, and none informs like an expert.

STUDYQURAN:35:13/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:13/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:35:13/r3.claim: On the Resurrection, the invoked deities disown the idolaters; 10:28 portrays them denying they were worshipped, as Satan also disavows the disbelievers.
STUDYQURAN:35:13/r3.anchor: They then disown the idolatry of the disbelievers, as in 10:28, where it is reported that they will say

STUDYQURAN:35:13/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:13/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:35:13/r4.claim: When all mankind is gathered, those worshipped besides God become enemies of their worshippers and deny their worship.
STUDYQURAN:35:13/r4.anchor: when mankind is gathered together, such will be enemies unto them and deniers of their worship

STUDYQURAN:35:13/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:13/r5.speaker: Aj, Q, Z
STUDYQURAN:35:13/r5.claim: No one can inform people as God informs them.
STUDYQURAN:35:13/r5.anchor: no one can inform you in the manner that God informs you (Aj, Q, Z)

STUDYQURAN:35:13/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:13/r6.speaker: Aj, Z, R
STUDYQURAN:35:13/r6.claim: In context, the phrase may mean that only God tells the truth about idols, especially matters of the Unseen that reason cannot deduce.
STUDYQURAN:35:13/r6.anchor: only God tells you the truth regarding this matter (Aj, Z), especially as it pertains to the Unseen and cannot be deduced through reasoning (R)

STUDYQURAN:35:13/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:13/r7.speaker: IK, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:35:13/r7.claim: The phrase may also refer to God's informing people about the events of the Day of Resurrection.
STUDYQURAN:35:13/r7.anchor: can also refer to the events on the Day of Resurrection (IK, Ṭ)

BURSEVI:v7p259/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p259/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p259/r1.claim: The ones invoked for help and relief from harm are idols.

BURSEVI:v7p259/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p259/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p259/r2.claim: Idols cannot hear because they are inanimate, and hearing is not a property of inanimate things.
BURSEVI:v7p259/r2.anchor: لأنهم جماد والجماد ليس من شأنه السماع

BURSEVI:v7p259/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p259/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p259/r3.claim: Even hypothetically hearing, they could not answer because they have no speech or cannot benefit anyone; one unable to benefit himself cannot benefit another.
BURSEVI:v7p259/r3.anchor: فإنهم لا لسان لهم أو ما أجابوكم لملتبسكم لعجزهم عن النفع بالكلية فإن من لا يملك نفع نفسه كيف يملك نفع غيره

BURSEVI:v7p259/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p259/r4.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v7p259/r4.claim: Al-Kashifi glosses this as their inability to bring benefits or avert harms.
BURSEVI:v7p259/r4.anchor: قال الكاشفي يعني : (قادر نيستند بر إيصال منافع ودفع مكاره)

BURSEVI:v7p259/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p259/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p259/r5.claim: On the Resurrection Day the idols will disavow being associated with God and being worshipped, saying, “You did not worship us.”
BURSEVI:v7p259/r5.anchor: يجحدون بإشراككم لهم وبعبادتكم إياهم بقولهم ما كنتم إيانا تعبدون

BURSEVI:v7p259/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p259/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p259/r6.claim: Rational pronouns are used because worshippers foolishly ascribed discernment to idols and because hearing and answering are predicated of them.
BURSEVI:v7p259/r6.anchor: لأن عبدتهم كانوا يصفونهم بالتمييز جهلا وغباوة ولأنه أسند إليهم ما يسند إلى أولي العلم

BURSEVI:v7p259/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p259/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p259/r7.claim: Alternatively, the objects of worship may include jinn and humans as well as idols, with rational beings predominating over idols in the wording.
BURSEVI:v7p259/r7.anchor: كل معبود من دون الله من الجن والإنس والأصنام فغلب غير الأصنام عليها

BURSEVI:v7p259/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p259/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p259/r8.claim: No informant matches God, who alone knows the inner reality of things; this confirms the truth about the idols and denies their divinity.
BURSEVI:v7p259/r8.anchor: وهو الحق سبحانه فإنه الخبير بكنه الأمور دون سائر المخبرين والمراد تحقيق ما أخبر به من حال آلهتهم

BURSEVI:v7p259/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p259/r9.speaker: صاحب لباب
BURSEVI:v7p259/r9.claim: The Lubab author says attributing a “likeness” to God is impermissible here; this is a common Arabic idiom for a reporter whose account is reliable in fact.
BURSEVI:v7p259/r9.anchor: صاحب لباب آورده كه اضافت مثل بخداى جائز نيست

BURSEVI:v7p259/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p259/r10.speaker: الزروقي
BURSEVI:v7p259/r10.claim: Al-Zarruqi defines the All-Aware as one who knows subtle matters others can reach only through testing and artifice.
BURSEVI:v7p259/r10.anchor: قال الزروقي : الخبير هو العليم بدقائق الأمور التي لا يتوصل إليها غيره إلا بالاختيار والاحتيال

BURSEVI:v7p259/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p259/r11.speaker: الغزالي
BURSEVI:v7p259/r11.claim: Al-Ghazali says no inward report is hidden from God: every movement, stillness, agitation, or tranquility in the dominion and kingdom is known to Him.
BURSEVI:v7p259/r11.anchor: وقال الغزالي : هو الذي لا يعزب عنه الأخبار الباطنة ولا يجري في الملك والملكوت شيء

TAB-FULL:v19p351/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p351/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p351/r1.claim: The idols are inanimate and do not understand what people say, so they cannot hear the invocation in the meaningful sense.
TAB-FULL:v19p351/r1.anchor: {إن تدعوهم لا يسمعوا دعاءكم ولو سمعوا ما استجابوا لكم} [فاطر: 14]

TAB-FULL:v19p351/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p351/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p351/r2.claim: Even if given hearing and made to understand the invocation, the idols could not answer because they cannot speak; hearing alone does not enable a reply.
TAB-FULL:v19p351/r2.anchor: وليس كل سامع قولا متيسرا له الجواب عنه

TAB-FULL:v19p351/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p351/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v19p351/r3.claim: Qatada says the idols would neither accept the invocation nor benefit the worshippers.
TAB-FULL:v19p351/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {إن تدعوهم لا يسمعوا دعاءكم ولو سمعوا ما استجابوا لكم} [فاطر: 14] «أي ما قبلوا ذلك عنكم

TAB-FULL:v19p351/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p351/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p351/r4.claim: The rebuke asks why people worship beings unable to benefit or harm them instead of worshipping God, who controls benefit and harm, created them, and blessed them.
TAB-FULL:v19p351/r4.anchor: يقول تعالى ذكره للمشركين به الآلهة والأوثان: فكيف تعبدون من دون الله من هذه صفته، وهو لا نفع لكم عنده، ولا قدرة له على ضركم

TAB-FULL:v19p351#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p351#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p351#2/r1.claim: On Judgment Day the idols will disown being treated as partners of God and repudiate their worshippers’ association of them with Him.

TAB-FULL:v19p351#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p351#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v19p351#2/r2.claim: Qatada says the idols will disown the association, refuse it, and not acknowledge it.
TAB-FULL:v19p351#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة {ويوم القيامة يكفرون بشرككم} [فاطر: 14] «إياهم، ولا يرضون، ولا يقرون به»

TAB-FULL:v19p351#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p351#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p351#2/r3.claim: Only God, whose knowledge encompasses what was and will be, can fully inform Muhammad about the idols’ and their worshippers’ fate and their disavowal at Judgment.
TAB-FULL:v19p351#2/r3.anchor: وذلك الخبير هو الله الذي لا يخفى عليه شيء كان أو يكون سبحانه

TAB-FULL:v19p351#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p351#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v19p351#2/r4.claim: Qatada says God is the expert who knows this disavowal will occur on Judgment Day.
TAB-FULL:v19p351#2/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {ولا ينبئك مثل خبير} [فاطر: 14] «والله هو الخبير أنه سيكون هذا منهم يوم القيامة»

TABATABAI:35:13-14/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:13-14/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:35:13-14/r9.claim: The idols cannot hear because they are insentient; their supposed lords, such as angels and holy human beings, are occupied with other matters and possess no independent hearing, hearing only when God enables it.
TABATABAI:35:13-14/r9.anchor: لأن الأصنام جمادات لا شعور لها ولا حس وأرباب الأصنام كالملائكة والقديسين من البشر في شغل شاغل

TABATABAI:35:14/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:14/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:35:14/r1.claim: The cited passage says Christ and the proximate angels do not disdain being servants of God; those who scorn worship will be gathered to him, supporting the dependence of alleged divine partners.
TABATABAI:35:14/r1.anchor: لن يستنكف المسيح أن يكون عبدا لله ولا الملائكة المقربون

TABATABAI:35:14/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:14/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:35:14/r2.claim: At resurrection the alleged partners disown the worship and shirk directed to them instead of acting as intercessors, as in the disavowal described in 2:166.
TABATABAI:35:14/r2.anchor: أي يردون عبادتكم إليكم ويتبرؤون منكم بدلا من أن يكونوا شفعاء لكم

TABATABAI:35:14/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:14/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:35:14/r3.claim: The verse’s denial that the invoked answer and its account of their later rejection correspond to the parallel passage the author cites from al-Ahqaf.
TABATABAI:35:14/r3.anchor: فالآية في نفي الاستجابة وكفر الشركاء يوم القيامة في معنى قوله

TABATABAI:35:14/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:14/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:35:14/r4.claim: The concluding address may be specifically to the Prophet after turning away from opponents who do not understand, or may use a particular address to mean any listener.
TABATABAI:35:14/r4.anchor: وهو خطاب خاص بالنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بعد الإعراض عن خطابهم لعدم تفقههم بالبيان الحق أو خطاب عام

TABATABAI:35:14/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:14/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:35:14/r5.claim: The author compares this address to similar second-person forms in 18:17–18.
TABATABAI:35:14/r5.anchor: في صورة الخطاب الخاص خوطب به السامع أي من كان

TABRISI:35:11-17/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:35:11-17/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:35:11-17/r9.claim: The idols cannot hear pleas for relief because they are inanimate and can neither benefit nor harm; even if God gave them hearing, they could not respond.
TABRISI:35:11-17/r9.anchor: { لا يسمعوا دعاءكم } لأنها جماد لا تنفع ولا تضر

TABRISI:35:11-17/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:35:11-17/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:35:11-17/r10.claim: On Resurrection God makes the idols speak to rebuke their worshippers and disown their worship, saying they never asked to be worshipped.
TABRISI:35:11-17/r10.anchor: ينطقهم الله يوم القيامة لتوبيخ عابديها فيقولون لم عبدتمونا وما دعوناكم إلى ذلك

TABRISI:35:11-17/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:35:11-17/r11.speaker: البلخي
TABRISI:35:11-17/r11.claim: Al-Balkhi allows the referent to be angels or Jesus: they do not hear the worshippers, or are too occupied to attend to them.
TABRISI:35:11-17/r11.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المراد به الملائكة وعيسى

TABRISI:35:11-17/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:35:11-17/r12.speaker: البلخي
TABRISI:35:11-17/r12.claim: Al-Balkhi also allows the referent to be idols: their disavowal manifests the worshippers' mistaken belief, as inert things glorify God by showing evidence of Him.
TABRISI:35:11-17/r12.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المراد به الأصنام ويكون ما يظهر من بطلان ما ظنوه

TABRISI:35:11-17/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:35:11-17/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:35:11-17/r13.claim: Only God, who knows everything, can fully inform of what brings benefit or harm and what is good or corrupting.
TABRISI:35:11-17/r13.anchor: أي لا يخبرك بما فيه الصلاح والفساد والمنافع والمضار مثل الله سبحانه العليم بالأشياء كلها

THALABI:v8p103/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p103/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p103/r4.claim: The idols do not hear their worshippers’ calls or answer them; on Judgment Day they disavow the worship and shirk.
THALABI:v8p103/r4.anchor: إن تدعوهم لا يسمعوا دعاءكم ولو سمعوا ما استجابوا لكم ويوم القيامة يكفرون بشرككم: يتبرؤون منكم ومن عبادتكم إياها

THALABI:v8p103/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p103/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p103/r5.claim: “None informs you like One fully aware” refers to God Himself.
THALABI:v8p103/r5.anchor: ولا ينبئك مثل خبير يعني نفسه تعالى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p412/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p412/r1.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p412/r1.claim: Muqatil says the false gods will disown the worship people directed to them on Judgment Day.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p412/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل: يتبرأون من عبادتكم إياها (¬7).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p412/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p412/r2.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p412/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the idols will say that people did not worship them, meaning they disown people associating them with God and did not command their worship.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p412/r2.anchor: وقال الزجاج: يقولون ما كنتم إيانا تعبدون، والمعنى: بإشراككم إياها مع الله في العبادة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p412/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p412/r3.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p412/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas and Muqatil identify the expert informer as God Himself: none knows His creatures better, and He knows the idols' coming disavowal.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p412/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومقاتل: يعني # نفسه عز وجل، يقول: فلا أحد أخبر منه بخلقه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p412/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p412/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p412/r4.claim: Abu Ishaq says only God knows and announces what will happen; al-Wahidi adds that none equals Him in knowledge, so there can be no informer like Him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p412/r4.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: لأن ما أنبأ الله -عز وجل- يكون فهو وحده يخبره ولا يشركه فيه أحد

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:12-14/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:12-14/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:12-14/r4.claim: On Resurrection Day, the beings worshipped as partners will disown the worshippers, saying that they were not worshipped by them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:12-14/r4.anchor: أي: يقولون: ما كنتم إيانا تعبدون

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:12-14/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:12-14/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:12-14/r5.claim: The expert who gives this true report is God, exalted is He.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:12-14/r5.anchor: ولا ينبئك مثل خبير } وهو الله عز وجل

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p782/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p782/r9.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p782/r9.claim: Here, calling the idols means calling out to them.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p783/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p783/r1.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p783/r1.claim: Al-Suddī glosses your duʿāʾ as your call or summons.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p783/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p783/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p783/r2.claim: Even if the idols heard, they would not answer; on Judgment Day they will disavow your associating them in worship.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p783/r2.anchor: {ولو سمعوا ما استجابوا لكم ويوم القيامة يكفرون بشرككم} [فاطر: 14] بعبادتكم إياهم

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p783/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p783/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p783/r3.claim: The fully informed one who can tell you is God.

ELMALILI:35:11-14/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:35:11-14/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:35:11-14/r16.claim: No one can inform as the All-Knowing God can; no one besides God grants prophethood.
ELMALILI:35:11-14/r16.anchor: Sana bir habîr gibi, yani Habîr olan Allah gibi haber veren olmaz, Allah’tan başkası peygamberlik veremez.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:14/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:14/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:14/r1.claim: Following the previous verse's statement that the beings worshipped besides God possess or control nothing, this verse concretely shows the absurdity of seeking help from them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:14/r1.anchor: kendilerinden medet umulmasının ne kadar abes olduğu somut bir anlatım tarzı ile açıklanmaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:14/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:14/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:14/r2.claim: The beings worshipped besides God do not hear their callers, cannot answer even if assumed to hear, and will disavow the attribution of divinity on Judgment Day with an ability God gives them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:14/r2.anchor: Onlar işitmezler, işittikleri varsayılsa bile karşılık veremezler; kıyamet günü de Allah’ın onlara vereceği bir yetenekle kendilerine yüklenen bu sıfatı tanımadıklarını beyan ederler.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:14/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:14/r3.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:14/r3.claim: Exegetes generally identify the beings worshipped here as idols.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:14/r3.anchor: Müfessirler genellikle bu varlıkları putlar olarak açıklamışlardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:14/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:14/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:14/r4.claim: Because the wording is general, it is better to include all beings treated as gods, such as humans, animals, the moon, and the sun.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:14/r4.anchor: âyetin ifadesi genel olduğu için kendilerine tanrı gözüyle bakılan insan, hayvan, ay, güneş gibi bütün varlıkların bu kapsamda düşünülmesi daha uygun görünmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:14/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:14/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:14/r5.claim: The point is not that a human fails to hear or answer as an ordinary person, but that these supposed gods cannot hear or answer worshippers' pleas from anywhere, whether secret or open, near or far.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:14/r5.anchor: gizli-açık, uzak-yakın nerede ve nasıl yalvarırlarsa yalvarsınlar kendilerine tapanları işitip cevaplayamamalarının kastedildiği söylenebilir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:14/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:14/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:14/r6.claim: The false gods' future disavowal is an unseen matter known only because God reports it, so no one can inform the Prophet as the all-aware God can.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:14/r6.anchor: Sözde tanrıların kıyamet günü kendilerine tapanlara karşı takınacakları tavır gayb kapsamında bir olay olduğu için bunu ancak Allah Teâlâ’nın haber vermesiyle biliriz

QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r1.claim: The worshipped beings cannot benefit others; at the Resurrection they disavow their worshippers’ association, but belief then is useless after the period of moral responsibility has ended.
QUSHAYRI:v3p64/r1.anchor: { ويوم القيامة يكفرون بشرككم } : لا يؤمنون إلا في ذلك الوقت ، ولكن لا ينفعهم الإيمان بعد زوال التكليف

BURHAN:v3p147/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p147/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p147/r5.claim: In the question whether the idols hear you when you call them, the implied object is your invocation, as the verse saying they do not hear your call confirms.
BURHAN:v3p147/r5.anchor: ﴿ هل يسمعونكم إذ تدعون ﴾ 6 أي هل يسمعون دعاءكم بدليل الآية الآخرى

BURHAN:v3p68#3/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p68#3/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p68#3/r5.claim: Zarkashi labels the close of the passage on powerless objects of worship a tadhyīl.
BURHAN:v3p68#3/r5.anchor: فقوله ﴿ ولا ينبئك مثل خبير ﴾ تذييل لاشتماله على

BURHAN:v4p372/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p372/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p372/r6.claim: The answer to conditional لو may itself be past in form, and it commonly takes the lām marker, as in the cited examples.
BURHAN:v4p372/r6.anchor: وجوابها يكون ماضيا لفظا كما سبق

BURHAN:v4p352/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p352/r1.speaker: ابن مالك
BURHAN:v4p352/r1.claim: Ibn Malik says لا resembling ليس may negate a whole class or something narrower, with context distinguishing the intended scope.
BURHAN:v4p352/r1.anchor: وقال ابن مالك في التحفة قد تكون المشبه ب ليس نافية للجنس ويفرق فيها بين إرادة الجنس وغيره بالقرائن

BURHAN:v4p352/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p352/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p352/r2.claim: When non-operating لا does not negate a whole class, the following noun is nominative as a topic and لا is repeated; examples include indefinite and definite nouns.
BURHAN:v4p352/r2.anchor: وأما غير العاملة فيرفع الاسم بعدها بالابتداء إذا لم يرد نفي العموم ويلزم التكرار

BURHAN:v4p352/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p352/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p352/r6.claim: With a conditional clause, لا can negate a future action; the idols will not hear the callers.
BURHAN:v4p352/r6.anchor: لأنه جزاء فلا يكون إلا مستقبلا

BURHAN:v2p359/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p359/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p359/r1.claim: Conditional forms include the simple particle إن, conditional nouns, and spatial or temporal forms; the compounds add meanings such as person, thing, place, or time.
BURHAN:v2p359/r1.anchor: الخامسة ادوات الشرط حروف وهي ان واسماء مضمنه معناها ثم منها ماليس بظرف كمن وما واي ومهما واسماء هي ظروف

BURHAN:v2p359/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p359/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p359/r5.claim: إن can serve certain or impossible premises: to prove a conditional consequence, speak tactfully and fairly, or portray a case that can exist only as a supposition; in 35:14 the pronoun refers to the idols.
BURHAN:v2p359/r5.anchor: ومنها تصوير ان المقام لا يصلح الا بمجرد فرض الشرط كفرض الشيء المستحيل كقوله تعالى ﴿ ولو سمعوا ما استجابوا لكم ﴾ 5 والضمير للاصنام

ITQAN:v3p198#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p198#2/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p198#2/r1.claim: A taḏyīl is a following sentence containing the first sentence’s meaning and confirming it, clarifying for those who missed it and consolidating for those who understood; this verse is an example.
ITQAN:v3p198#2/r1.anchor: وهو أن يؤتى بجملة عقب جملة والثانية تشتمل على المعنى الأول لتأكيد منطوقه أو مفهومه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p2/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p2/r1.claim: Reordering the opening of Imruʾ al-Qays’s poem turns eloquent verse into nonsense and severs its attribution, showing that its identity depends on a particular arrangement of words.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p2/r1.anchor: منزل قفا ذكرى من نبك حبيب

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p2/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p2/r2.claim: The meaningful composition of words follows meanings arranged in the mind according to reason; sentence roles impose ordering, such as an interrogative’s precedence and an adjective’s following its noun.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p2/r2.anchor: المعنى الذي له كانت هذه الكلم بيت شعر أو فصل خطاب هو ترتيبها على طريقة معلومة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p2/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p2/r3.claim: When critics praise wording as sweet or elegant, they are not judging its sounds or basic lexical form but an effect in the heart and a distinction produced by the intellect.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p2/r3.anchor: ليس ينبئك عن أحوال ترجع إلى أجراس الحروف وإلى ظاهر الوضع اللغوي بل إلى أمر يقع من المرء في فؤاده

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p2/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p2/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p2/r4.claim: Word choice can also be praised independently of meaning when it is familiar in current usage rather than strange or vulgar; sometimes the fault called vulgarity belongs to the meaning instead.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p2/r4.anchor: اللفظة مما يتعارفه الناس في استعمالهم ويتداولونه في زمانهم ولا يكون وحشيا غريبا أو عاميا سخيفا

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p88/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p88/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p88/r1.claim: The highest compositional merit appears when the parts form one integrated construction; paired similes by Imruʾ al-Qays, al-Farazdaq, and Bashshār illustrate this crafted correspondence.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p88/r1.anchor: فاعلم أنه النمط العالي ، والباب الأعظم ، والذي لا ترى سلطان المزية يعظم في شيء كعظمه فيه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p88/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p88/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p88/r2.claim: Al-Jurjānī finds Ziyād al-Aʿjam’s sea comparison still more remarkable because its construction is subtler and its interweaving more unusual.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p88/r2.anchor: وإنما كان أعجب لأن عمله أدق ، وطريقه أغمض ، ووجه المشابكة فيه أغرب

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p88/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p88/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p88/r3.claim: Some passages require little compositional thought: they merely string parallel phrases together, like beads, without forming a new overall image or structure.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p88/r3.anchor: بل ترى سبيله في ضم بعضه إلى بعض سبيل من عمد إلى لآل فخرطها في سلك لا يبغي أكثر من أن يمنعها التفرق

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p378/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p378/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p378/r1.claim: Metaphor, allusion, representation, figurative speech, and concision are pillars of eloquence and Qurʾānic inimitability; al-Jurjānī cites Qurʾānic examples, including this verse, to show their centrality.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p378/r1.anchor: أنها الأقطاب التي تدور البلاغة عليها

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p378/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p378/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p378/r2.claim: The claim that the Qurʾān’s inimitability lies in easy-to-pronounce letters would require accusing scholars of error; the alternative that rhetorical devices make letters easy is absurd.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p378/r2.anchor: فيزعم أن الوصف الذي كان له القرآن معجزا هو سلامة حروفه مما يثقل على اللسان

DAMGHANI:v1p173/r2.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p173/r2.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p173/r2.claim: Duʿāʾ can mean calling or invoking; idols do not hear their callers.
DAMGHANI:v1p173/r2.anchor: الثالث : الدعاء يعني النداء قوله تعالى في سورة القمر

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p292/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p292/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p292/r1.claim: Duʿāʾ is a request from someone lower to someone higher to obtain something; its verb is daʿā, yadʿū, duʿāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p292/r1.anchor: الدعاء : ( هو ) طلب الأدنى من الأعلى تحصيل الشيء . يقال منه : دعوت ، أدعو ، دعاء .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p292/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p292/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p292/r2.claim: Duʿwa denotes one instance; food invitation uses fatḥa and lineage uses kasra.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p292/r2.anchor: والدعوة : المرة الواحدة . والدعوة إلى الطعام بالفتح ، وفي النسب بالكسر .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p292/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p292/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p292/r3.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says this is most Arab usage except among ʿAdī al-Ribāb, who reverse the vowels.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p292/r3.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة : وهذا أكثر كلام العرب إلا عدي الرباب فإنهم ينصبون الدال في النسب ويكسرونها في الطعام .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p292/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p292/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p292/r4.claim: The hadith phrase about the milk’s caller names the first little trickle that calls forth the milk after it.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p292/r4.anchor: وفي الحديث : ( دع داعي اللبن ) . وهو القليل ينزل في الضرع ليدعو ما بعدها .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p292/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p292/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p292/r5.claim: Tadāʿat al-ḥīṭān means the walls collapsed; dawāʿī al-dahr means time’s vicissitudes.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p292/r5.anchor: وتداعت الحيطان : تهادمت . ودواعي الدهر : صروفه .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p292/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p292/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p292/r6.claim: Duʿāʾ can mean speech, including what people say when punishment comes and in Paradise.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p292/r6.anchor: أحدها : القول . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأعراف : ﴿ فما كان دعواهم إذ جاءهم بأسنا ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p292/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p292/r7.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p292/r7.claim: Duʿāʾ can mean worship, including worship of others besides God.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p292/r7.anchor: والثاني : العبادة . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأنعام : ^ ( قل أندعوا من دون الله ما لا ينفعنا ولا يضرنا ) ^

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p292/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p292/r8.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p292/r8.claim: Duʿāʾ can mean calling aloud, including the present verse and the deaf not hearing a call.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p292/r8.anchor: والثالث : النداء . ومنه قوله تعالى [ في بني إسرائيل ] : ^ ( يوم يدعوكم فتستجيبون بحمده ) ^

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p292/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p292/r9.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p292/r9.claim: Duʿāʾ can mean seeking aid, as in commands to summon witnesses or helpers and Pharaoh’s challenge to Moses.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p292/r9.anchor: والرابع : الاستعانة . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة : ^ ( وادعوا شهداءكم من دون الله ) ^

NAHHAS:v3p367/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p367/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p367/r4.claim: The clause is conditional with its result; the following law clause carries the sense of the first even though law is not normally used for a conditional result.
NAHHAS:v3p367/r4.anchor: فيه معنى الأول وإن كانت لولا يجازى بها

NAHHAS:v3p367/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p367/r5.speaker: قتادة
NAHHAS:v3p367/r5.claim: Qatāda explains their failure to respond as their not following or accepting the callers.
NAHHAS:v3p367/r5.anchor: قال قتادة ما استجابوا لكم ما تبعوكم ولا قبلوا منكم

NAHHAS:v3p367/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p367/r6.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v3p367/r6.claim: Abū Isḥāq says the false gods will say that their worshippers were not worshipping them.
NAHHAS:v3p367/r6.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق أي يقولون ما كانوا إيانا يعبدون

NAHHAS:v3p367/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p367/r7.speaker: قتادة
NAHHAS:v3p367/r7.claim: Qatāda says God has informed people that this disavowal will occur on the Day of Resurrection.
NAHHAS:v3p367/r7.anchor: قال قتادة الله جل وعز أخبر أنه يكون هذا منكم يوم القيامة

SAMIN-DURR:35:14/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:35:14/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:35:14/r1.claim: شرككم is a verbal noun annexed to its agent.

ZAJJAJ:v4p266/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p266/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p266/r4.claim: The idols will say that their worshippers did not worship them, disowning the worship directed to them.
ZAJJAJ:v4p266/r4.anchor: المعنى يقولون: ما كنتم إيانا تعبدون، فيكفرون بعبادتكم إياهم

ZAJJAJ:v4p266/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p266/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p266/r5.claim: The expert who informs the Prophet is God, since only God knows and reports what will happen.
ZAJJAJ:v4p266/r5.anchor: وهو الله، لأن ما أنبأ الله به مما يكون فهو وحده يخبره، لا يشركه فيه أحد

ASAD-NOTES:35:13#n13/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:35:13#n13/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:35:13#n13/r1.claim: False objects of worship, including saints, angels, relics, fetishes, and deified natural forces, will disown their worshippers on Resurrection Day; this symbolizes humanity's final perception of ultimate reality.
ASAD-NOTES:35:13#n13/r1.anchor: will 'bear witness" against their one-time worshippers on Resurrection Day, and will "disown" them

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p342/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p342/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p342/r5.claim: Istajāba lahu means that someone responded to a person or listened to that person's invocation.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p342/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p342/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p342/r6.claim: The deities' helplessness is plain in this world and will be clearer in the Hereafter: they will not hear invocations in distress, and even if they hear, cannot answer.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p342/r6.anchor: The verse points out the helplessness and baselessness of their deities:

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p342/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p342/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p342/r7.claim: The deities the idolaters invented never existed, so they could neither hear worshippers nor answer their prayers.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p342/r7.anchor: The deities which the Idolaters worshipped

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p342/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p342/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p342/r8.claim: If worshipped beings actually existed, the righteous among them, such as angels and prophets, will openly disown their worshippers.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p342/r8.anchor: the righteous among them like the angels and the prophets

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p342/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p342/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p342/r9.claim: Evil beings such as jinn and devils will tell their worshippers that their choice was their misfortune and that they cannot help them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p342/r9.anchor: The evil among those worshipped like the jinn and the devils

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p342/r10.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p342/r10.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p342/r10.claim: The deities were unaware of being invoked for help in this life and could not answer the idolaters.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p342/r10.anchor: these deities were unaware that in this world

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p343/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p343/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p343/r1.claim: On the Day of Judgment, the deities will reject that they were worshipped as associates with God, confirming their inability to answer their worshippers.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p343/r1.anchor: on the Day of Judgement they will reject they were worshipped as associated deities to God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p343/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p343/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p343/r2.claim: Islahi connects the denial of worship to 34:40-41, where angels deny being worshipped and say that people actually worshipped the jinn.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p343/r2.anchor: The details of this rejection have been cited in Sūrah Sabā’ thus:

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p343/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p343/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p343/r3.claim: The indefinite khabīr is left without a definite article to convey the magnitude of the one truly cognizant.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p343/r3.anchor: The word ریِبَخ is not defined by an definite particle to portray its magnitude.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p343/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p343/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p343/r4.claim: Only a real knower can disclose hidden matters that will later appear; people should heed this admonition rather than remain captive to fancies.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p343/r4.anchor: only a real cognizant being knows what is hidden from the eyes of people and which will one day manifest before them.

NASHR:v1p454/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p454/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p454/r1.claim: When a hamza in these waw or yāʾ contexts has no separate written shape, the rasm can reflect gemination, a dialect that drops hamza, or allow both retaining and deleting it.
NASHR:v1p454/r1.anchor: على لغة من يسقط الهمزة رأسا، أو لتحتمل القراءتين إثباتا وحذفا

NASHR:v1p454/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p454/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p454/r3.claim: For a hamza with ḍamma after kasra, as in wa-lā yunabbiʾuka and sanaqriʾuka, the rasm uses yāʾ according to al-Akhfash rather than the customary waw.
NASHR:v1p454/r3.anchor: فلم يرسم على مذهب الجادة بواو، بل رسم على مذهب الأخفش بالياء

NASHR:v1p454/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p454/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p454/r4.claim: The converse forms suʾila and suʾilū are written by the customary rule rather than al-Akhfash’s rule.
NASHR:v1p454/r4.anchor: ورسم عكسه سئل وسئلوا على مذهب الجادة

NASHR:v1p454/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p454/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p454/r5.claim: Manuscripts vary on these open hamzas after fatḥa: some retain alif as expected, while most omit it for simplification when its place is clear.
NASHR:v1p454/r5.anchor: فرسمت في بعض المصاحف بالألف على القياس، وحذفت في أكثرها على غير قياس

NASHR:v1p454/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p454/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p454/r6.claim: Codices differ on retaining or omitting hamza in arayta and related forms; though some restrict deletion to Sūrat al-Dīn or one other form, Ibn al-Jazarī prefers applying the variation throughout the Qurʾān.
NASHR:v1p454/r6.anchor: والصحيح إجراء الخلاف في الجميع، والله أعلم

NASHR:v1p454/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p454/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p454/r7.claim: The rasm of naʾā uses only nūn and alif to permit both readings; the fixed alif represents hamza, while the inflected alif is deleted when the two alifs meet.
NASHR:v1p454/r7.anchor: فإنه رسم بنون وألف فقط؛ ليحتمل القراءتين

NASHR:v1p454/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p454/r8.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p454/r8.claim: Rāʾ is written with alif as hamza’s shape; in two Najm occurrences an added yāʾ reflects the imāla pronunciation.
NASHR:v1p454/r8.anchor: وكذلك رأى كتب في جميع القرآن براء وألف لا غير

NASHR:v1p484/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p484/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p484/r4.claim: A third deletion face based on some codices is invalid for ashmazzat, iṭmaʾannū, amlaʾanna, and related forms; al-Kisāʾī’s sound report for arayta does not transfer to other readers.
NASHR:v1p484/r4.anchor: فقد حكي فيها وجه ثالث، وهو الحذف على رسم بعض المصاحف، وليس بصحيح

NASHR:v1p484/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p484/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p484/r5.claim: An open hamza after kasra or ḍamma is replaced by the corresponding long vowel in one valid face; the reported between-between facilitation is unsound.
NASHR:v1p484/r5.anchor: وأما المفتوح بعد كسر وبعد ضم فلا إشكال في إبدال همزته

NASHR:v1p484/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p484/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p484/r6.claim: For hamza with ḍamma after fatḥa in raʾūf and tuʾizzuhum, the single valid face is between-between; the reported waw-with-ḍamma alternative based on rasm is invalid.
NASHR:v1p484/r6.anchor: ونحوه فيه وجه واحد، وهو بين بين

NASHR:v1p484/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p484/r9.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p484/r9.claim: With hamza after kasra and ḍamma, the majority use between hamza and waw; al-Akhfash’s yāʾ substitution is preferred by al-Dānī and others following the rasm.
NASHR:v1p484/r9.anchor: أحدهما بين بين، أي: بين الهمزة والواو على مذهب سيبويه

NASHR:v1p484/r10.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p484/r10.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p484/r10.claim: Facilitation between hamza and yāʾ and replacement by waw are cited but rejected; al-Dānī prefers deletion with ḍamma before waw where hamza is followed by waw.
NASHR:v1p484/r10.anchor: وهو الوجه المعضل كما تقدم، وحكي وجه رابع

NASHR:v1p484/r11.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p484/r11.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني
NASHR:v1p484/r11.claim: Al-Dānī and readers following the rasm prefer deletion with ḍamma on the preceding letter when hamza is followed by waw.
NASHR:v1p484/r11.anchor: وهو المختار عند أبي عمرو الداني، ومن أخذ باتباع الرسم

NASHR:v1p484/r12.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p484/r12.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p484/r12.claim: Using kasra before the waw is a weak face; of the six proposed readings, only three are sound, including facilitation between hamza and waw and deletion options.
NASHR:v1p484/r12.anchor: وذكر فيه كسر ما قبل الواو، وهو الوجه الخامل

NASHR:v1p484/r13.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p484/r13.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p484/r13.claim: When stopping creates two consecutive sukūns in forms like yastahziʾūn, any valid reading may take madd, tawassuṭ, or qaṣr.
NASHR:v1p484/r13.anchor: فيجوز في كل وجه من الأوجه المذكورة كل من الثلاثة الأوجه من المد والتوسط والقصر

NASHR:v1p484/r14.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p484/r14.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p484/r14.claim: Abū al-ʿIzz al-Qalānisī reports replacing the hamza with waw in yuʾdihi and analogues; Ibn al-Jazarī says this face is baseless.
NASHR:v1p484/r14.anchor: ذكره أبو العز القلانسي، وقال ليس بشيء

ALUSI-FULL:v22p182/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p182/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p182/r1.claim: This resumes and confirms the preceding argument by exposing the true state of those invoked.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p182/r1.anchor: إستئناف مقرر لما قبله كاشف عن جلية حال ما يدعونه

ALUSI-FULL:v22p182/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p182/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p182/r2.claim: For idol worshippers, idols cannot hear because lifeless objects have no capacity for hearing.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p182/r2.anchor: بأنه جماد ليس من شأنه السماع هذا إذا كان الكلام مع عبدة الأصنام

ALUSI-FULL:v22p182/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p182/r3.speaker: البلخي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p182/r3.claim: If the invoked include Jesus or other close servants, their not hearing may result from being occupied and far from the caller.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p182/r3.anchor: وبعد بعيد عن عابده كعيسى عليه السلام وروى هذا عن البلخي

ALUSI-FULL:v22p182/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p182/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p182/r4.claim: He has no transmitted proof that angels or sanctified souls hear appeals from non-idolatrous callers; reason permits it but cannot establish it.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p182/r4.anchor: إذ لم أظفر بدليل سمعي على ذلك والعقل يجوزه لكن لا يكتفي بمجرد تجويزه في القول به

ALUSI-FULL:v22p182/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p182/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p182/r5.claim: Hypothetical hearing does not entail a spoken answer, since idols lack speech; alternatively, they cannot act at all and cannot benefit callers.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p182/r5.anchor: لأنهم لم يرزقوا قوة التكلم والسماع لا يستلزم ذلك فالمراد بالإستجابة الإستجابة بالقول

ALUSI-FULL:v22p182/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p182/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p182/r6.claim: For close servants, verbal response is impossible because callers falsely treat them as deities; practical aid is not their duty.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p182/r6.anchor: فكيف يجيبون زاعم ذلك فيهم وفيه من التهمة ما فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v22p182#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p182#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p182#2/r1.claim: The previous rationale, that answering would diminish servitude, may also explain their refusal to act.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p182#2/r1.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون هذا تعليلا للأول أيضا فتأمل

ALUSI-FULL:v22p182#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p182#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p182#2/r2.claim: At Resurrection idols disown the worshippers' association, either by speaking after God enables them or through an unmistakable display of their state.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p182#2/r2.anchor: يجحدون إشراككم إياهم وعبادتكم إياهم وذلك بأن يقدر الله تعالى الأصنام على الكلام

ALUSI-FULL:v22p182#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p182#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p182#2/r3.claim: Dhu al-Rummah's speaking ruins illustrate how lifeless stones may seem to address someone through their condition, supporting disavowal by state.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p182#2/r3.anchor: وقفت على ربع لمية ناطق يخاطبني آثاره وأخاطبه وأسقيه

ALUSI-FULL:v22p182#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p182#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p182#2/r4.claim: If the invoked are angels or other close servants, their repudiation is clear; the preceding sura depicts angels denying that polytheists worshipped them.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p182#2/r4.anchor: وقد حكى الله تعالى قول الملائكة للمشركين في السورة السابقة

ALUSI-FULL:v22p182#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p182#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v22p182#2/r5.claim: Qatada and others identify the uniquely informed reporter as God, who knows the reality of things; this confirms the idols' non-divinity.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p182#2/r5.anchor: يعني به تعالى نفسه كما روى عن قتادة وغيره فإنه سبحانه الخبير بكنه الأمور

ALUSI-FULL:v22p182#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p182#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p182#2/r6.claim: The address may apply to any listener: no informant equals the all-knowing expert whose knowledge omits nothing in earth or heaven.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p182#2/r6.anchor: لا يخبرك أيها السامع كائنا من كنت مخبر هو مثل الخبير

ALUSI-FULL:v22p182#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p182#2/r7.speaker: إبن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v22p182#2/r7.claim: Ibn Atiyya suggests the idols themselves are expert informants since they disclosed that they are not gods; al-Alusi calls this far-fetched.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p182#2/r7.anchor: يحتمل أن يبكون ذلك من تمام ذكر الأصنام كأنه قيل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418/r3.claim: The idols do not hear their invocations, and even if they heard, they would not answer them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418/r3.anchor: يعني: إن تدعو الأصنام، {لا يسمعوا دعاءكم ولو سمعوا ما استجابوا لكم}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418/r4.claim: At the Resurrection the idols will disown their worshippers and their worship, saying that the worshippers did not worship them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418/r4.anchor: يتبرؤون منكم ومن عبادتكم إياها، يقولون: ما كنتم إيانا تعبدون.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418/r5.claim: The “all-knowing expert” is God Himself; no one can inform the Prophet as one who knows all things does.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418/r5.anchor: يعني: نفسه أي: لا ينبئك أحد مثلي خبير عالم بالأشياء.

BAYDAWI-FULL:35:13-14/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:13-14/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:13-14/r5.claim: The idols are inanimate and cannot hear their worshippers.

BAYDAWI-FULL:35:13-14/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:13-14/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:13-14/r6.claim: Even if they could hear, they could not benefit the worshippers; alternatively, they would disown them and their worship.
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:13-14/r6.anchor: أو لتبرئهم منكم مما تدعون لهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:35:13-14/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:13-14/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:13-14/r7.claim: On Judgment Day the idols will acknowledge the falsity of the association, or say, “You were not worshipping us.”
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:13-14/r7.anchor: بإشراككم لهم يقرون ببطلانه أو يقولون

BAYDAWI-FULL:35:13-14/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:13-14/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:13-14/r8.claim: No informer matches the truly knowledgeable God; the verse confirms His account of the idols and refutes the claims made for them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:13-14/r8.anchor: فإنه الخبير به على الحقيقة دون سائر المخبرين

BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r3.claim: Whether invoked in worship or for help, the inanimate objects cannot hear their worshippers at any time.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r3.anchor: أي المعبودات من دونه دعاء عبادة أو استغاثة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r4.claim: Even if they heard, they would not answer because they would know that granting the requests displeases God; they had refused the trust rather than act against His pleasure.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r4.anchor: لأنهم إذ ذاك يعملون أن إجابتكم لا ترضي الله , وهم مما أبى أن يحمل الأمانة ويخون فيها

BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r5.claim: Alternatively, even granting hearing, it does not entail speech or the ability to fulfill a request; this reading includes living beings worshipped, since animals hear and answer while responders may lack the requested capacity.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r5.anchor: ولو فرض أنه يوجد لهم سمع , أو ولو كانوا سامعين - ليدخل فيه من عبد من الأحياء - ما لزم من السماع إجابة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r6.claim: When God makes the objects speak on Judgment Day, they will deny the association people made with them and disown it.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r7.claim: The discourse turns away from those who neither admit nor properly understand or follow the warning, addressing instead someone capable of full understanding and obedience.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r7.anchor: صرف الخطاب عنهم إلى من له الفهم التام والطاعة الكاملة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r8.claim: No one gives an account as authoritative as the all-knowing God; His report cannot be challenged, while other reports invite criticism.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p213/r8.anchor: أي بالغ الخبر , فلا يمكن الطعن في شيء مما أخبر به , وأما غيره فلا يخبر خبرا إلا يوجه إليه نقص

DURR-FULL:v7p14/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p14/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p14/r8.claim: Qatada says the idols neither hear worshippers’ calls nor accept them if they did; at the Resurrection they will disown the worship, and God, the All-Informed, knows this will happen.
DURR-FULL:v7p14/r8.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {إن تدعوهم لا يسمعوا دعاءكم ولو سمعوا ما استجابوا لكم} أي ما قبلوا ذلك منكم {ويوم القيامة يكفرون بشرككم} قال: لا يرضون ولا يقرون به

DURR-FULL:v7p14/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p14/r9.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v7p14/r9.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the addressees’ objects of worship as idols: they cannot hear calls or provide good, and at the Resurrection they disown their worship.
DURR-FULL:v7p14/r9.anchor: عن السدي في قوله {إن تدعوهم لا يسمعوا دعاءكم} قال: هي الآلهة لا تسمع دعاء من دعاها وعبدها من دون الله تعالى {ولو سمعوا ما استجابوا لكم} قال: ولو سمعت الآلهة دعاءكم ما استجابوا لكم بشيء من الخير

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3177#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3177#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3177#2/r1.claim: Qatādah says the objects of worship will neither accept nor acknowledge the worshippers’ association on Judgment Day; God, the All-Knowing, knows this will happen.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3177#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : ان تدعوهم لا يسمعوا دعاءكم ولو سمعوا ما استجابوا لكم اي ما قبلوا ذلك منكم

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3177#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3177#2/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3177#2/r2.claim: Al-Suddī identifies the objects as idols that cannot hear; even if they heard, they could not bring their worshippers any good, and “your association” means worshipping them.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3177#2/r2.anchor: عن السدى في قوله : ان تدعوهم لا يسمعوا دعاءكم قال : هي الالهة لا تسمع دعاء من دعاها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p282/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p282/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p282/r5.claim: The conditional sentence is a second predicate of ‘those you invoke besides Him.’
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p282/r5.anchor: وجملة { إن تدعوهم } خبر ثان عن { الذين تدعون من دونه }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p282/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p282/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p282/r6.claim: The claim that idols do not hear alerts polytheists to their incapacity; it is not itself the proof, since they believed the idols heard and addressed them with praise.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p282/r6.anchor: والمقصد منها تنبيه المشركين إلى عجز أصنامهم بأنها لا تسمع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p282/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p282/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p282/r7.claim: The ‘even if they heard’ clause coordinates with the preceding clause; the waw is not parenthetical, and the hearing is hypothetical for argument’s sake.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p282/r7.anchor: فإنها معطوفة على جملة { إن تدعوهم لا يسمعوا دعاءكم }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p282/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p282/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p282/r8.claim: Even supposing the idols heard, they would not answer or grant requests; repeated unanswered prayers before visible idols show incapacity or incomprehension, since their worshippers cannot be faulted as unworthy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p282/r8.anchor: فطالما دعوا الأصنام فلم يسمعوا منها جوابا وطالما دعوها فلم يحصل ما دعوها لتحصيله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p283/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p283/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p283/r1.claim: Istijāba may mean answering a caller with words or granting a petitioner what was requested; Ibn ʿĀshūr calls this use of a shared word in both senses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p283/r1.anchor: وقوله : { ما استجابوا } يجوز أن يكون بمعنى إجابة المنادي بكلمات الجواب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p283/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p283/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p283/r2.claim: The same verb may also mean responding to a petitioner by giving the requested thing; he calls this use of a shared term in both meanings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p283/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون بمعنى إجابة السائل بتنويله ما سأله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p283/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p283/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p283/r3.claim: The verse completes the exposure of idols by saying God will make them speak in the afterlife and disavow the worshippers’ association of them with God, including any invitation to or approval of idolatry.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p283/r3.anchor: بأن تلك الأصنام ينطقها الله فتتبرأ من شركهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p283/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p283/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p283/r4.claim: Kufr here means repudiation or denial accompanied by aversion.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p283/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p283/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p283/r5.claim: The possessive attributes the shirk to its human perpetrators: their associating the idols with God in divinity.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p283/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p283/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p283/r6.claim: Calling the idols by a rational relative pronoun and rational pronouns treats them as people, mockingly following the polytheists’ own framing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p283/r6.anchor: على تنزيل الأصنام منزلة العقلاء مجاراة للمردود عليهم على طريقة التهكم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p284/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p284/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p284/r1.claim: The closing maxim authenticates the preceding reports: their speaker knows them and no one can inform the hearer as well.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p284/r1.anchor: تذييل لتحقيق هذه الأخبار بأن المخبر بها هو الخبير بها وبغيرها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p284/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p284/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p284/r2.claim: The verse uses ‘inform’ because nabaʾ denotes news of an important, momentous event.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p284/r2.anchor: وعبر بفعل الإنباء لأن النبأ هو الخبر عن حدث خطير مهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p284/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p284/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p284/r3.claim: The address is for anyone able to hear the saying: the sentence is cast as a general proverb rather than directed to one particular person.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p284/r3.anchor: لأن هذه الجملة أرسلت مرسل الأمثال فلا ينبغي تخصيص مضمونها بمخاطب معين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p284/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p284/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p284/r4.claim: Khabīr is an intensive adjective from knowing something with certainty; it denotes the class of those truly expert in it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p284/r4.anchor: و { خبير } صفة مشبهة مشتقة من خبر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p284/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p284/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p284/r5.claim: The proverb’s brevity omits the objects of ‘inform’ and ‘expert’ and the dimension of likeness, all recoverable from context.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p284/r5.anchor: فحذف منه متعلق فعل ( ينبىء ) ومتعلق وصف { خبير }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p284/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p284/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p284/r6.claim: Although the intended expert is the speaker, khabīr is indefinite to generalize under negation; denying any equal informer implies no one informs as he does, and identifies him through the maxim.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p284/r6.anchor: فالمعنى : ولا ينبئك بهذا الخبر مثلي لأني خبرته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p284/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p284/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p284/r7.claim: Mathl means an equal in amount, hence ‘double,’ or an equal in quality, hence ‘similar’; the latter is a rare faʿl pattern for an active participle, like shibh, nidd, and khidn.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p284/r7.anchor: والمثل بكسر الميم وسكون المثلثة : المساوي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434/r6.speaker: جمهور الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434/r6.claim: The majority read tadʿūhum with second-person tāʾ.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434/r7.speaker: الحسن ويعقوب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434/r7.claim: Al-Hasan and Yaʿqub read yadʿūna with third-person yāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434/r7.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ويعقوب «يدعون» بالياء من تحت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434/r10.claim: The idols’ nullity is first shown by their inability to hear prayer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434/r10.anchor: أولها أنها لا تسمع إن دعيت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434/r11.claim: Even if idols heard, they would not answer; this anticipates the contrived objection that they might hear.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434/r11.anchor: والثاني أنها لا تجيب أن لو سمعت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434/r12.claim: The third sign is that idols disavow their worshippers on Judgment Day.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434/r12.anchor: والثالث أنها تتبرأ يوم القيامة من الكفار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434/r13.claim: The worshippers’ shirk is attributed to idols because worshippers established them as partners; the verbal noun is attached to its agent.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434/r13.anchor: فأضاف الشرك إليهم من حيث هم قرروه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434/r14.claim: One possibility is spoken disavowal, with God giving idols the cognition required to speak.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434/r14.anchor: وقوله يكفرون يحتمل أن يكون بكلام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434/r15.claim: Alternatively, disavowal is figurative: idols remain inert while speakers move and argue; Dhu al-Rumma’s ruined-dwelling poem illustrates the usage.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434/r15.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون بما يظهر هناك من جمودها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434/r16.speaker: قتادة وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434/r16.claim: Commentators including Qatada say the expert is God, whose truthful report guarantees the outcome.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434/r16.anchor: قال المفسرون قتادة وغيره «الخبير» هنا أراد به تعالى نفسه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434/r17.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434/r17.claim: Alternatively, this continues the idols’ testimony: no informant is like one reporting about itself, and idols testify against their worshippers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434/r17.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون قوله ولا ينبئك مثل خبير من تمام ذكر الأصنام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p481#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p481#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p481#3/r1.claim: The objects worshipped are inanimate, so they cannot hear their worshippers' prayers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p481#3/r1.anchor: لأنهم جماد ولو سمعوا بأن يخلق الله لهم أسماعا ما استجابوا لكم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p481#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p481#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p481#3/r2.claim: Even if God gave them hearing, they would still have no capacity to answer their worshippers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p481#3/r2.anchor: ولو سمعوا بأن يخلق الله لهم أسماعا ما استجابوا لكم أي لم يكن عندهم إجابة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p481#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p481#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p481#3/r3.claim: On Judgment Day the false gods will disown their worshippers' association of partners with God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p481#3/r3.anchor: ويوم القيامة يكفرون بشرككم أي يتبرؤون من عبادتكم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p481#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p481#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p481#3/r4.claim: The expert is God Himself, who knows all things and is the most reliable source about what He says will happen.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p481#3/r4.anchor: ولا ينبئك يا محمد مثل خبير أي عالم بالأشياء يعني نفسه عز وجل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p540#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p540#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p540#2/r8.claim: The idols do not hear invocations because they are inanimate objects with no souls.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p540#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p540#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p540#2/r9.claim: Even if the idols heard, they would be unable to fulfill what their worshippers ask.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p540#2/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p540#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p540#2/r10.claim: On Judgment Day the alleged deities disown their worshippers, as in 46:5–6 and 19:81–82, where false gods fail to answer and become enemies of their worship.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p540#2/r10.anchor: {ويوم القيامة يكفرون بشرككم} ، أي: يتبرؤون منكم، كما قال تعالى: {ومن أضل ممن يدعو من دون الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p541/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p541/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p541/r1.claim: No one can inform you as fully as an expert about the outcomes, final consequences, and eventual destination of affairs.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p541/r1.anchor: ولا يخبرك بعواقب الأمور ومآلها وما تصير إليه، مثل خبير بها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p541/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p541/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p541/r2.claim: Qatada says the expert is God Himself, whose report of what will occur is certain.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p541/r2.anchor: قال قتادة: يعني نفسه تبارك وتعالى، فإنه أخبر بالواقع لا محالة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p615/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p615/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p615/r1.claim: The idols do not hear their invocation because they are inanimate.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p615/r1.anchor: إن تدعوا الأوثان { لا يسمعوا دعاءكم } لأنهم جماد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p615/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p615/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p615/r2.claim: Even hypothetically hearing the prayer, idols would not answer because they do not claim the divinity people assign them and disavow it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p615/r2.anchor: لأنهم لا يدعون ما تدعون لهم من الإلاهية ، ويتبرؤون منها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p615/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p615/r3.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p615/r3.claim: An alternative explanation is that the idols would not benefit their worshippers.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p615/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p615/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p615/r4.claim: No informant equals an expert who knows the matter; only such an expert can tell its truth accurately.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p615/r4.anchor: ولا يخبرك بالأمر مخبر هو مثل خبير عالم به

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p615/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p615/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p615/r5.claim: God's account of the idols is true because He alone is expert in the matter He reports.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p615/r5.anchor: والمعنى : أن هذا الذي أخبرتكم به من حال الأوثان هو الحق

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p615/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p615/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p615/r6.claim: The verb is read with either yāʾ or tāʾ: يدعون or تدعون.

MUQATIL:35:13-14/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:35:13-14/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:35:13-14/r6.claim: The idols do not hear their invocations, and even if they could hear, they would not answer.
MUQATIL:35:13-14/r6.anchor: يقول: لو أن الأصنام سمعوا ما استجابوا لكم

MUQATIL:35:13-14/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:35:13-14/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:35:13-14/r7.claim: On Resurrection Day the idols disown their worshippers and say they never told them to worship them.
MUQATIL:35:13-14/r7.anchor: يقول: إن الأصنام يوم القيامة يتبرءون من عبادتكم إياها، فتقول للكفار: ما أمرناكم بعبادتنا

MUQATIL:35:13-14/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:35:13-14/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:35:13-14/r8.claim: The expert who informs is God Himself; none is better informed than He is.
MUQATIL:35:13-14/r8.anchor: يعني الرب نفسه سبحانه فلا أحد أخبر منه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#2/r1.claim: The ones invoked are idols, and as inanimate objects they cannot hear prayers.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#2/r2.claim: Even if they could hear, the idols would not answer, since they do not claim divinity and disavow it.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#2/r3.claim: On Judgment Day idols will disown their association and worship, saying their worshippers did not worship them.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#2/r3.anchor: ﴿ ويوم القيامة يكفرون بشرككم ﴾ باشراككم لهم وعبادتكم اياهم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#2/r4.claim: No informant explains these causes of delusion like God, who knows hidden matters; the expert alone tells the truth, and God is expert here.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p339#2/r4.anchor: ولا يخبرك بالأمر مخبر هو مثل خبير عالم به يريدان الخبير بالأمر وحده هو الذى يخبرك بالحقيقة

QURTUBI-FULL:35:14/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:14/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:35:14/r1.claim: If people call on the idols for help in hardship, the idols cannot hear because they are inanimate and neither see nor hear.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:14/r1.anchor: أي إن تستغيثوا بهم في النوائب لا يسمعوا دعاءكم لأنها جمادات لا تبصر ولا تسمع

QURTUBI-FULL:35:14/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:14/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:35:14/r2.claim: Even if they heard, hearing alone does not make every hearer able to speak or answer.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:14/r2.anchor: إذ ليس كل سامع ناطقا. وقال قتادة: المعنى لو سمعوا لم ينفعوكم

QURTUBI-FULL:35:14/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:14/r3.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:35:14/r3.claim: Qatada explains that even if the idols heard, they would not benefit their worshippers.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:14/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة: المعنى لو سمعوا لم ينفعوكم

QURTUBI-FULL:35:14/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:14/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:35:14/r4.claim: Another hypothetical view says that even if given life and understanding, the idols would be more obedient to God than their worshippers and would not answer a call to disbelief.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:14/r4.anchor: وقيل: أي لو جعلنا لهم عقولا وحياة فسمعوا دعاءكم لكانوا أطوع لله منكم

QURTUBI-FULL:35:14/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:14/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:35:14/r5.claim: On Judgment Day the objects of worship will deny that their worshippers worshipped them and disavow them.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:14/r5.anchor: أي يجحدون أنكم عبدتموهم، ويتبرءون منكم. ثم يجوز أن يرجع هذا إلى المعبودين

QURTUBI-FULL:35:14/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:14/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:35:14/r6.claim: The reference may include beings capable of understanding—angels, jinn, prophets, and devils—who deny that worship was right or that they ordered it, as Jesus says in the cited verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:14/r6.anchor: مما يعقل كالملائكة والجن والأنبياء والشياطين أي يجحدون أن يكون ما فعلتموه حقا

QURTUBI-FULL:35:14/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:14/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:35:14/r7.claim: The reference may also include idols: God will resurrect them so they can testify that they were unworthy of worship.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:14/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن يندرج فيه الأصنام أيضا، أي يحييها الله حتى تخبر أنها ليست أهلا للعبادة

QURTUBI-FULL:35:14/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:14/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:35:14/r8.claim: The “all-knowing expert” is God: no one knows God's creation better than God, so no one can inform you about His work as He does.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:14/r8.anchor: هو الله جل وعز أي لا أحد أخبر بخلق الله من الله، فلا ينبئك مثله في عمله
